ev.q: Among 1,288 Michigan residents who were monitored for signs and symptoms after potential HPAI A(H5N1) virus exposure, 53 (4.1%) reported signs and symptoms
Twenty (6.5%) exposed workers reported symptoms and were tested for influenza A(H5) virus infection.
Two dairy workers received positive test results (3.8% of all persons tested, <1% of all monitored dairy workers).
Among 1,288 Michigan residents who were monitored for signs and symptoms after potential HPAI A(H5N1) virus exposure, 53 (4.1%) reported signs and symptoms
Eighteen (2.1%) symptomatic persons were identified and tested; all test results were negative for influenza A(H5).
Among seven affected commercial poultry facilities, 857 persons exposed to affected birds were identified.

public_health_question.v: How many persons exposed to HPAI A(H5N1)-infected animals in Michigan were monitored, developed symptoms, were tested and were identified as cases?

ev.q: This report describes response activities in Michigan, which led to detection of the second and third human cases related to the 2024 HPAI A(H5N1) outbreak.
Health Monitoring, Testing, and Case Identification Among Persons Exposed to Influenza A(H5N1) — Michigan, 2024
Before the onset of mild unilateral conjunctivitis, the patient reported direct ocular exposure to raw, unpasteurized milk from an affected cow.
Active symptom monitoring and testing of exposed workers led to detection of the second and third known dairy-associated HPAI A(H5N1) cases in 2024.
Workers at 12 (60%) of those dairies were enrolled in text-based daily symptom monitoring

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is reported; occupation (dairy, poultry workers) is a route of exposure, not SES.

notes: Symptom and testing percentages are reported separately for dairy workers, poultry workers and other exposed persons but never contrasted, so they are treated as summaries rather than a comparison. RT-PCR testing only confirms case status and is not a procedure. Design inferred as surveillance/descriptive (active monitoring); none is named.
